hypotheses.paper: 1°, second sentence (l.523–524; l.586 « P = φ̃⁻¹(D ∩ φ̃(V)) »), the full form
hypotheses.note: P = p ⁻¹' (demiEspace z ∩ range p) for every developing map p equal to φ on P, proved: for every shell (poche_eq_preimage_of_coque_proj), in every dimension n ≤ 1 (poche_eq_preimage_of_le_one_proj), for P = V (poche_eq_preimage_of_eq_univ_proj, which contains z ≡ 0), and when range p ∩ H̊ is star-shaped in the affine space H̊ about a point of cote < 1 (poche_eq_preimage_of_starConvex_proj). Not proved for the remaining pockets (ConnexeOuvertPrinted, OQ-71).

hypotheses.paper: (ii) range p ∩ H̊ star-shaped about a point c of H̊ with z(c) < 1
hypotheses.note: Not a hypothesis of the paper: a sufficient condition for the full form, stated as its own lemma (the roadmap block's case (ii)), to delimit OQ-71. Every shell meets it (exists_starConvex_of_coque_proj).

findings: 1°c, full form (statement l.523–524; proof l.585–590): it holds for every shell (Déf. 2, l.188–190), in every dimension. By 3° (l.528–529, proof l.600–603), φ̃(V) is a convex part of S(n). For M ∈ φ̃⁻¹(D ∩ φ̃(V)) and N ∈ P, both images lie in H̊, so the segment between them lies in H̊ and in the convex D, and it lies in φ̃(V): the « ligne brisée » of l.588 can be one segment, and the printed argument closes. The paper proves 3° after 1°c, but 3°'s proof uses only Prop. 7's corollary and the chart, never 1°c, so there is no circularity (poche_eq_preimage_of_coque_proj; with 2°–4°, theoreme_poche_balayable_coque_proj; printed, theoremeCoquePrinted n for every n).

1°c, full form, in dimension n ≤ 1: the Theorem holds as printed, the full form included (theoremePrinted_of_le_one_proj; premierPrinted_of_le_one_proj; connexePrinted_of_le_one_proj). Every pocket is then a shell (isCoqueProj_of_le_one_proj): H̊ is an affine line or a point, and φ(P), connected, is convex. So the shell case applies. Neither the transcription (l.181–190, l.517–533) nor the proof makes this observation.

1°c, full form, for P = V: trivially true, since P ⊆ φ̃⁻¹(D) always (poche_eq_preimage_of_eq_univ_proj). This contains the constant cote z ≡ 0 (poche_eq_preimage_of_cote_eq_zero, which gives P = V); conversely P ≠ V forces a non-constant cote (not_cote_eq_zero_of_ne_univ_proj).

1°c, full form, when φ̃(V) ∩ H̊ is star-shaped, in the affine space H̊ (Déf. 6), about a point c of D (z(c) < 1): D ∩ φ̃(V) is then star-shaped about c, so connected, which is what l.588 presumes (poche_eq_preimage_of_starConvex_proj). Special cases: φ̃(V) ∩ H̊ convex in H̊ (poche_eq_preimage_of_isAffConvex_proj) and φ̃(V) a convex part of S(n) (poche_eq_preimage_of_isConvexPart_proj). This is the projective twin of the affine poche_eq_preimage_of_starConvex_affine.

OQ-71 sharpened (not ruled): the printed full form is equivalent to its open case, ConnexePrinted n ↔ ConnexeOuvertPrinted n (connexePrinted_iff_ouvert_proj), and TheoremePrinted n ↔ ConnexeOuvertPrinted n (theoremePrinted_iff_ouvert_proj). ConnexeOuvertPrinted n asks that D ∩ φ̃(V) be connected for the pockets that are not shells, are not all of V (so have a non-constant cote), and for whose chart φ̃(V) ∩ H̊ is star-shaped about no point of D. It holds vacuously for n ≤ 1 (connexeOuvertPrinted_of_le_one_proj). So the full form is open only for a non-shell pocket with a non-constant cote, in dimension n ≥ 2, and more sharply only for a pocket P ≠ V that is not a shell and whose φ̃(V) ∩ H̊ is star-shaped about no point of D. It is neither proved nor refuted there; no counterexample was found or formalised.
questions: OQ-71 is not resolved here: the component form of 1°c (theoremeComposantePrinted) or the full form (TheoremePrinted). Reading taken: none. The row stays closed up to OQ-71 and nothing is marked. The REPORT gives the sharpened form for the master to record (findings, last entry). Two wordings are offered, the roadmap's coarse one and the formal ConnexeOuvertPrinted; which one OQ-71 records is the master's choice.

« star-shaped » in case (ii), which is the roadmap's condition and not the paper's, is read in H̊'s affine structure (Déf. 6) as ∀ y ∈ φ̃(V) ∩ H̊, affineSegment c y ⊆ φ̃(V) ∩ H̊, with c ∈ H̊ and z(c) < 1. Read in S(n) instead (segments closedSeg c y ⊆ φ̃(V) for all y ∈ φ̃(V)), it implies this one when c ∈ H̊, because the segments of S(n) between two points of H̊ are its affine segments (Sphere.coe_image_affineSegment). The weaker H̊ form is taken, so the lemma is the stronger one.

kb_proposals: In dimension n ≤ 1 every projective pocket is a shell (isCoqueProj_of_le_one_proj, Chapter2/PremierFull.lean). φ(P) is connected in H̊ ≅ ℝⁿ, so it is convex: transport it through e : H̊ ≃ᵃ ℝⁿ (Sphere.nonempty_hemi_affineEquiv), whose inverse is an open embedding into S(n) (isOpenEmbedding_coe_affineEquiv), and apply convex_of_isPreconnected_of_le_one (PremierAffine). Any n ≤ 1 statement about pockets then reduces to shells, with no arc argument on S(1).

A part W of H̊ that is star-shaped (affineSegment ℝ c y ⊆ W) about one of its points is connected in S(n) (isPreconnected_coe_image_of_starConvex_proj). Transport through e : H̊ ≃ᵃ ℝⁿ with affineSegment_image and affineSegment_eq_segment, apply StarConvex.isPathConnected, then take the image by fun y => (e.symm y : S n). demiEspace z ∩ A is the image of {q | z q < 1 ∧ ↑q ∈ A} (demiEspace_inter_eq_image_proj).
The trace on H̊ of a convex part of S(n) is affinely convex in H̊, with no k ⊆ H̊ hypothesis (isAffConvex_preimage_of_isConvexPart_proj); Sphere.isConvexPart_iff_isAffConvex needs k ⊆ H̊.

OQ-71's open part is ConnexeOuvertPrinted n (PremierFull.lean): a pocket that is not a shell, P ≠ V, and φ̃(V) ∩ H̊ star-shaped about no point of D. connexePrinted_iff_ouvert_proj reduces ConnexePrinted n to it, and it is empty for n ≤ 1. A counterexample to the full form must live there, in dimension n ≥ 2. One P ⊆ Ω ∖ {z = 1} is a whole component, and no segment of Ω joins P to another component of D ∩ Ω (condition b); this is where to look.
